# Decision closure with stored inventory and joint calibration moments

Internal derivations by decision_closure, 2026-10-15. Source repository pin:
`846f185763ed3a27310fad4ce9471ba324d1e5f4`.

No laboratory measurements, independently validated reactor model or historical
novelty claim is supplied. Dissipativity, generalized moment duality, support
optimization and optimal linear-estimator allocation are established methods.
The contribution here is the explicit combined contract, exact model bound,
counterexample and reproducible decision/cost calculation.

## 1. A dynamic class missed by steady-mode convex closure

Consider a normalized stored reactive inventory x in (0,1), constant positive
adsorption coefficient a, and positive conversion coefficient b(t):

\[
 \dot x=a(1-x)-b(t)x,\qquad r(t)=b(t)x.                       \tag{1}
\]

There are two declared dark modes, b0<b1, with
\(b(t)=b_0+D u(t)\), D=b1-b0 and u(t) in {0,1}. The normalized metered
running cost is u; an affine nonzero base cost can be restored. Assume a
hot-duty budget \(\int_0^T u\,dt\le fT\). Define
\(\bar b=b_0+Df\) and

\[
 C(f)=\frac{a\bar b}{a+\bar b}.                              \tag{2}
\]

**Theorem 1.** Every measurable, possibly state-dependent or randomized
switching schedule satisfies, pathwise conditional on its control realization,

\[
 \int_0^T r\,dt\le T C(f)+V_p(x(0))-V_p(x(T)),\qquad
 V_p(x)=x-p\log x,\quad p=\left(\frac{a}{a+\bar b}\right)^2.   \tag{3}
\]

For cyclic inventory x(T)=x(0), the average is at most C(f). This bound is
sharp for the ideal binary class with arbitrarily fast, cost-free switching:
periodic schedules with duty f approach C(f). The limit is a relaxed-control
supremum, not an experimentally acquired waveform. If a constant intermediate
b=bar b is available at the same full cost, it already attains this value.

**Proof.** For every p>0,

\[
 r-pb+\dot V_p=a(1-x)(1-p/x),\qquad
 a(1-\sqrt p)^2-a(1-x)(1-p/x)
 =a\frac{(x-\sqrt p)^2}{x}\ge0.                             \tag{4}
\]

Integrate, use \(\int b\le T\bar b\), and minimize
\(p\bar b+a(1-\sqrt p)^2\). Its minimizer is the p in (3) and its value
is (2). For binary periods h with fixed duty f, the exact segment flow is
\(x_{out}=a/(a+b)+(x_{in}-a/(a+b))e^{-(a+b)t}\). The periodic state converges
to a/(a+bar b) as h tends to zero, so the mean reward converges to C(f). QED.

## 1. Exact criterion: decision identification is weaker than mechanism identification

Let `theta` denote an admissible physical world. A declared action `a` has utility `J_theta(a)`, complete resource cost `c_theta(a)`, and feasibility `c_theta(a)<=B`. An experiment supplies a response record `y=h(theta)`. Let `A*(theta)` be the set of optimal feasible actions. For a finite action class, an exact decision based only on `y` exists if and only if

    intersection_{theta:h(theta)=y} A*(theta) is nonempty

for every response fiber that can occur.

Necessity: the decision rule must choose one action that is optimal in every world yielding that same record. Sufficiency: choose a common optimizer in each fiber. With finite actions, a fixed tie-breaking order gives an explicit rule. A unique mechanism need not be identified; all worlds in a fiber may have different microscopic descriptions and the same optimal action.

For a strict superiority claim between an illuminated action and a declared dark comparator class, define

    Delta(theta)=J_theta(light)-sup_{a in dark,c_theta(a)<=B}J_theta(a).

An exact response record certifies strict superiority uniformly over its compatible worlds precisely when `inf_{theta:h(theta)=y}Delta(theta)>0`. With uncertainty, replace the response fiber by a valid simultaneous confidence set. The same idea supplies a sufficient finite-precision margin; no particular inference terminology closes a fiber that still contains opposite decisions.

This criterion is about a specified action class, budget, horizon and population. A mechanism claim, a universal thermal-only exclusion, an optimum over untested control histories and a decision over a measured finite library are different questions.

## 1. A complete affine-direction amplitude certificate

Let Ω be bounded Lipschitz, F:R^(m×n)→R a rank-one-convex homogeneous quartic polynomial, B a constant matrix, c a constant target translation, and

    u0(x)=Bx+c,   u(x)=a(x)u0(x),   a=1 on ∂Ω.

Initially take a smooth; the result extends by strong W1,4 approximation. No rotational invariance, positivity of a, mass constraint, nonvanishing u0 or special phase equation is required. Positive a literally preserves the unit direction; signed a preserves the pointwise affine line and is an additional consequence of the direct even-quartic polynomial proof. Define P=DF(B), Q=u0⊗∇a and

    R_F(C,Q)=F(C+Q)−F(C)−DF(C):Q.

Then the pointwise identity is

    F(Du)−F(B)
      =R_F(aB,Q)+div[((a^4−1)/4) P^T u0].                 (1)

Indeed Du=aB+Q, F(aB)=a^4F(B), DF(aB)=a^3P, and Euler gives P:B=4F(B). Differentiating the displayed flux gives exactly `(a^4−1)F(B)+a^3P:Q`. The boundary flux vanishes because a=1. Q has rank at most one, so integrating gives

    ∫[F(Du)−F(B)] ≥0.                                    (2)

Use the supplied quartic scalar remainder lemma, independently reconstructed: a convex quartic `At^4+Lt^3+C2t²+Dt+E` has C2≥3L²/(8A), hence its t=1 tangent remainder is at least A/3. If A=0, global convexity forces L=0 and C2≥0. Therefore, with

    μ_F=min{F(R):rank R=1, |R|=1},

equation (1) strengthens to

    ∫[F(Du)−F(B)] ≥(1/3)∫F(Q)
                     ≥(μ_F/3)∫|u0|^4|∇a|^4.             (3)

The polynomial identity also covers zeros of u0, avoiding a singular phase chart. For bounded Ω, multiplication by u0 is continuous on W1,4, so the extension is direct. For a general positively p-homogeneous F and positive a, the same identity has `(a^p−1)/p`; the real signed-amplitude version above uses even quartic polynomial homogeneity.
